metaDescription: Odoo for NGOs: why there is no fund accounting, how grants and restricted funds are really built on analytic plans, and what donor audits ask for.
intro: Odoo ships no fund accounting. There is no restricted fund ledger, no automatic release of restricted income, no fund balance carried forward and no inter-fund entry. What Odoo does ship is double-entry accounting, analytic plans, budgets, projects, timesheets, purchase agreements, expense claims, surveys and a website that can take a payment. An NGO system is those parts arranged so every transaction carries the grant, the programme and the expense classification it belongs to. That arrangement is the project.

The edition line is worth settling early. Community gives you the accounting core, analytic accounting with several plans at once, budgets, Projects, Timesheets, Expenses, Purchase Agreements, Events, Surveys and Email Marketing. Enterprise adds the dynamic financial report builder, consolidation, currency revaluation of open balances, Documents, Sign, Approvals, Planning, Subscriptions and Payroll. One funder and one currency runs happily on Community. A multi-donor portfolio in four currencies will fight Community reporting every single month.

The rest of the work is coding structure and discipline, and it decides whether the build survives its first donor audit. Analytic plans have to be designed before the first vendor bill. Every expense line has to carry a distribution. A grant budget runs on the award period, not your fiscal year. And Odoo will let a user post restricted money against the wrong fund without a warning, because nothing in the software knows the money was restricted.
whoFor: National and international NGOs running several donor-funded awards at once, each with its own budget, period, currency and report format.
Foundations and grant-making trusts that need awards tracked as commitments and disbursement tranches rather than as ordinary purchases.
Faith-based and community organisations collecting regular giving, issuing numbered receipts and running one or two programmes.
Social enterprises with a trading arm funding charitable work, where the two sets of books have to stay apart for tax reasons.
Not for organisations that need certified fund accounting on day one, because Odoo has no fund ledger and never has had one.
Not for a two-person charity with a single bank account, where a bookkeeping package costs a fraction and answers the same questions.

capabilities.title: Grants, funds and donors as analytic plans
capabilities.body: From Odoo 17 onward several analytic plans apply at once, and a journal item carries a percentage distribution against each. A typical NGO build runs four: fund or award, programme, donor budget line, and office or country. One salary line then reports in four directions without a single extra account. Applicability rules can force a plan to be filled on vendor bills. The statutory chart of accounts stays short, which is the point.

capabilities.title: Budgets against an award, and what they will not do
capabilities.body: Odoo sets planned amounts against analytic accounts for a date range and reports actual against plan. It reports. It does not block: nothing stops a bill posting past an exhausted budget line. Award budgets also run on the grant period, so a 30 month award needs its own range rather than the fiscal year. The budget model has changed between recent Odoo versions, so confirm what your target version ships before designing grant control on it.

capabilities.title: Restricted income and release to the programme
capabilities.body: Restricted money usually arrives before it is spent, and Odoo will not release it for you. The pattern that works is a deferred income account per restricted fund, with income recognised by journal entry as qualifying spend posts, the analytic distribution carrying the fund on both sides. Somebody runs that entry each period. Where the donor recognises on receipt instead, the fund balance is simply the analytic balance and you need a report that shows it per fund.

capabilities.title: Staff time and salary split across awards
capabilities.body: Timesheets in Community post against the analytic distribution on the task and value at the employee hourly cost, which is one rate per person and excludes employer burden unless you build it in. That produces cost per award without any payroll module. Payroll itself is Enterprise and depends on a local payroll localisation existing at all. Donors want a signed monthly timesheet showing the percentage per award; Odoo holds the hours, the certified sheet is a printed report.

capabilities.title: Procurement that survives a donor audit
capabilities.body: Purchase Agreements in Community records a call for tender with several vendor bids against one requirement, which is exactly the evidence a three-quote threshold rule needs, and the RFQ, comparison, order, receipt and bill stay linked. The Approvals app is Enterprise; in Community the equivalent control is the purchase double validation limit plus record rules. Vendor due diligence and anti-terrorism screening documents attach to the vendor contact and can be made mandatory by a checklist field.

capabilities.title: Donations, regular giving and receipting
capabilities.body: The Odoo website includes a donation payment block that takes an arbitrary amount through a configured payment provider, and the providers available depend on your country. It records the money. It does not create a donor record with consent, a statutory receipt series, a fund allocation or a thank-you sequence, and those four are the actual deliverables. Recurring monthly giving uses Subscriptions on Enterprise, or a saved payment token charged by a scheduled action.

capabilities.title: Beneficiaries, field data and monitoring
capabilities.body: There is no beneficiary model in Odoo. A beneficiary is a contact, or a dedicated model with its own record rules where the data is sensitive enough to keep away from general staff. Surveys captures structured responses but needs connectivity, so field teams normally stay on ODK, KoboToolbox or CommCare and the cleaned results are pushed in over the API. Indicator targets against actuals is a reporting build, not a configuration setting.

setup.title: Design the analytic plans before the first bill
setup.body: Fix the plans and the code structure in week one: award, programme, budget line, office. Build the donor own budget line reference into the analytic code so a report can be produced in the donor format without a mapping table maintained by hand. Adding a plan later is easy. Back-filling a distribution onto eight thousand posted journal items is not, and half-coded history turns every grant report into a manual reconciliation.

setup.title: Make the distribution mandatory, not optional
setup.body: Analytic plan applicability can set a plan as mandatory for a company, an account prefix or a document type, so a vendor bill without an award cannot be validated. Turn that on before go-live, not after. Then default a distribution on the product, on the project and on the employee, so most coding happens without anyone thinking about it and only the exceptions reach a human at validation time.

setup.title: Two layers: statutory accounts, functional classification
setup.body: The chart of accounts follows the local statutory chart and nothing else. Programme, management and fundraising classification belongs on a second analytic plan, because the same salary account splits across all three and duplicating accounts to solve it produces a chart nobody can close. Agree the allocation basis, headcount or floor area or recorded time, in writing before go-live, and post it as a recurring journal so the split is reproducible.

setup.title: Multi-currency: decide what the award is measured in
setup.body: A grant awarded in euros and spent in local currency needs the award currency held on the grant record, a rate policy agreed with the donor covering award rate or monthly rate or transaction rate, and a decision about who absorbs the difference. Odoo posts realised exchange differences on reconciliation in both editions. Revaluation of open foreign currency balances comes from the Enterprise reporting engine, so Community projects handle it as a manual period entry.

setup.title: Opening balances and the awards already running
setup.body: Migrate the trial balance, open payables and receivables and the fund balance per award as opening entries at a period end cut-off. Do not attempt to reload years of historical transactions; nobody reads them and they carry every coding error the old system had. For awards mid-term, load spend to date per budget line from the last financial report the donor approved, so the burn rate is right from the first day rather than the first quarter.

pitfalls.title: Odoo will not stop restricted money being spent wrongly
pitfalls.body: Nothing in the software knows a fund is restricted. An analytic balance can go negative, a bill can be coded to an award that closed last year, and the trial balance still balances because analytic accounting sits alongside the ledger rather than inside it. The controls are procedural: mandatory distribution, closed awards archived so they cannot be selected, and a monthly report of spend against remaining budget per award that somebody is actually required to read.

pitfalls.title: The analytic ledger and the general ledger drift apart
pitfalls.body: A distribution can be left blank, coded sixty forty by accident, or edited after the entry is posted. Reconcile analytic totals against the expense accounts every single month and chase the difference in the month it appears. Finding a two percent gap during a donor audit two years in costs more in staff time and eligibility risk than the entire system did, and it is the finding that gets a grant partially disallowed.

pitfalls.title: Shared costs allocated once and never again
pitfalls.body: Rent, the finance officer, the vehicle and the internet line get split across awards in a spreadsheet in month one. Then an award closes, another starts, and the spreadsheet is not updated for a year. Build the allocation as a recurring template journal entry with a documented basis, review it at every award start and close, and attach the working paper to the entry. Auditors ask to see the basis, not the number.

pitfalls.title: Donor reports in a format Odoo does not produce
pitfalls.body: Institutional donors want a fixed template: budget line, approved budget, this period, cumulative, variance, in the award currency, with a narrative column. The built-in reports will not get you there and neither will an analytic pivot pasted into a spreadsheet each quarter. Scope and price a report build at the start. This is the single most under-estimated item on NGO projects, and it is the one the finance team judges the system by.

pitfalls.title: Beneficiary data treated as ordinary contacts
pitfalls.body: Names, identity numbers, phone numbers and photographs of vulnerable people sitting in the contacts table are readable by anyone with contact access and exportable in two clicks, and anything typed into the chatter is pushed out in follower notification emails. Put sensitive fields on a model with its own record rules, remove the export right from users who do not need it, and set a retention rule, because Odoo deletes nothing on its own.

pitfalls.title: One database for the charity and the trading arm
pitfalls.body: Multi-company holds two legal entities in one database with separate journals, chart and fiscal positions, but contacts and products are shared and users switch between them with a menu. Recharges have to be posted on both sides or the entities never agree. Where the trading subsidiary is taxable and the charity is not, get the tax mapping reviewed before go-live: that mistake is a tax exposure, not a reporting inconvenience.

worksWith: Odoo Accounting with several analytic plans, the backbone of every grant report
Project and Timesheets for programme activity and staff time charged to awards
Purchase Agreements for the multiple-quote thresholds donors impose
Expenses for field office claims coded to an award at the point of entry
Surveys for structured assessment forms where the team has connectivity
ODK, KoboToolbox or CommCare for offline field collection, pushed in over the API
Website payment providers and the donation block for online and regular giving
Documents, Sign, Approvals and Payroll on Enterprise for agreements, authorisation trails and staff pay

regional.note: The Charity SORP under FRS 102 requires a Statement of Financial Activities with restricted, unrestricted and endowment fund columns. Odoo produces no SOFA, so the fund columns come from analytic plans and the statement itself is built or exported. Gift Aid is claimed through HMRC Charities Online against a declaration per donor, which Odoo does not track, and VAT-registered charities file under Making Tax Digital with partial exemption.

ASC 958 splits net assets into with and without donor restrictions, and Form 990 needs every expense classified across programme services, management and general, and fundraising. That functional split is a second analytic plan applied to every line, not a set of accounts. Federal awards under 2 CFR 200 add an indirect cost rate, either negotiated or the ten percent de minimis, applied to a defined base.

A gemeinnuetzig organisation has to account separately for four spheres, the ideal sphere, asset management, the special purpose operation and the commercial operation, because only the last is taxed. That is an analytic plan agreed with the Steuerberater before go-live. Donation receipts follow the officially prescribed Zuwendungsbestaetigung wording, books must satisfy GoBD retention, and the accountant will expect a DATEV export rather than a PDF.

Foreign contributions fall under FCRA and must be received into the designated account at the SBI New Delhi main branch, held apart from domestic funds and never mixed, with quarterly disclosure and the FC-4 annual return. Domestic 80G giving requires Form 10BD by 31 May and a Form 10BE certificate to each donor, so donor PAN and address have to be captured at receipt, not chased in April.

International organisations sign an MoU with the Economic Affairs Division while local bodies register with the provincial authority, and both carry reporting obligations with them. Tax approval under section 2(36) and the 100C credit depend on filing on time and on audited accounts. Where the organisation earns consultancy or training income, that arm faces provincial sales tax on services and FBR digital invoicing.

An association or foundation files its annual beyanname through the DERBIS system by the end of April, and public benefit status is a separate grant. Any trading activity has to run through a separate economic enterprise, the iktisadi isletme, which keeps its own books, registers for VAT and corporate tax and falls under e-Fatura and e-Arsiv once thresholds are met. Two entities, one organisation, one database.

Non-profits are licensed and supervised by the National Center for the Non-Profit Sector, with the platform reporting that comes with it. A pure donation is outside the scope of VAT because nothing is supplied in return, while a sponsorship carrying branding or a paid event ticket is a taxable supply. Once registered, the entity sits inside ZATCA Phase 2, and staff are paid through WPS.

A public benefit entity is exempt from corporate tax only where it is listed in the relevant Cabinet Decision, and it still has to register and file rather than ignore the regime. VAT follows the substance: an unconditional grant with no supply is outside scope, while sponsorship, ticketed events and consultancy income are standard rated. Mainland staff are paid through the Wage Protection System.

faqs.a: No. Neither Community nor Enterprise ships a fund ledger, an automatic release of restricted income or a fund-level balance sheet. Funds are modelled as an analytic plan, which reports well and enforces nothing. If a regulator or auditor requires a balanced balance sheet per fund with due-to and due-from entries between funds, that is a development item and it belongs in the scope before the contract is signed.

faqs.q: Community or Enterprise for an NGO?
faqs.a: The dividing line is reporting and process apps. Community covers accounting, analytic plans, budgets, Projects, Timesheets, Expenses, Purchase Agreements, Events and Surveys. Enterprise adds the dynamic financial report builder, consolidation, currency revaluation, Documents, Sign, Approvals, Planning, Subscriptions and Payroll. One funder in one currency runs on Community. A multi-donor, multi-currency portfolio spends the licence and saves more than that on report development.

faqs.q: Can Odoo produce a report in our donor's own template?
faqs.a: Not out of the box. Analytic reporting gives budget against actual by award and budget line as a pivot. Turning that into the donor template, with the award currency, cumulative columns and their line codes, is a report build. Coding the analytic accounts with the donor budget line references at setup removes most of the mapping work and makes the build much cheaper.

As employee records without a contract or payroll where you need hours, or as contacts where you do not. Employee records consume no user licence, so a volunteer register costs nothing in subscription terms. Published shift rosters are Planning, an Enterprise app; attendance check-in is Community. Odoo ships no volunteer application, screening or background-check workflow, so that part is configuration or a custom model.

faqs.q: Can we take donations on the website?
faqs.a: Yes. The website includes a donation payment block that accepts an arbitrary amount through a configured payment provider, and which providers are available depends on your country. What it does not create is a donor record with consent, a numbered statutory receipt, a fund allocation or an acknowledgement sequence. Those four are the build, and they are what the fundraising team will actually judge the system on.

faqs.q: How many paid users will we need?
faqs.a: Only staff logging into the back office. Portal users are free in both editions, so partner organisations, board members and grantees viewing documents, a project or an invoice cost nothing. That usually decides the field office question: give field staff a portal view and a form rather than a back office seat, and keep paid users for finance, programme management and procurement.

faqs.q: Is there a grant management module?
faqs.a: No. In practice an award is a project or an analytic account with a start date, an end date, a budget, a currency and an owner. Deliverable deadlines are activities or tasks with due dates, and the reporting calendar is a set of recurring tasks. It works well and it is genuinely useful, but it is configuration you have to design, not an app you install.

faqs.q: Can the charity and its trading company share one system?
faqs.a: Yes, through multi-company: separate journals, chart, taxes and fiscal positions per entity, with contacts and products shared. Consolidated reporting across the two is an Enterprise app. Recharges must be posted on both sides or the entities never reconcile, and where one is taxable and the other is not, have the tax mapping reviewed before go-live rather than at the first audit.
